definitions.title: The Concavity Test
definitions.statement: If f''(x) > 0 for all x on an interval, the graph of f is concave upward (lies above its tangent lines). If f''(x) < 0, the graph is concave downward (lies below its tangent lines).
conditions: f is twice differentiable on the interval
definitions.explanation: f'' > 0 means the derivative f' is increasing (tangent slopes become more positive).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Positive second derivative means bowl holds water (concave up).

definitions.title: Point of Inflection
definitions.latex: (c, f(c)) \quad \text{where concavity changes sign and tangent line exists}
definitions.statement: A point (c, f(c)) on a curve is a point of inflection if f is continuous there and the curve changes from concave up to concave down, or from concave down to concave up.
conditions: Concavity strictly changes sign across c
definitions.explanation: At an inflection point, f''(c) = 0 or f''(c) does not exist (and the tangent line crosses the curve).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Inflection points are where the curve transitions between curving upward and downward.

definitions.title: The Second Derivative Test for Local Extrema
definitions.latex: f'(c) = 0 \text{ and } f''(c) < 0 \implies \text{Local Max}; \quad f'(c) = 0 \text{ and } f''(c) > 0 \implies \text{Local Min}
definitions.statement: Suppose f''(x) is continuous near c with f'(c) = 0. If f''(c) < 0, f has a local maximum at c. If f''(c) > 0, f has a local minimum. If f''(c) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
definitions.explanation: If f''(c) = 0, revert to the First Derivative Test.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Negative second derivative at critical point -> local maximum.
